chapters.name: Logic, Sets and Real Number System

questions.text:
Which of the following sentences are the statements? Find the truth values of those sentences which are statements:
a) Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal.
b) Nepal exports oil.
c) 3 + 5 = 8
d) Where do you live?
e) Understand logic.
f) Oh! how beautiful the scene is?
questions.source_solution:
a) The given sentence is a declarative sentence. So, it is a statement and its truth value is True (T).
b) The given sentence is a declarative sentence. So, it is a statement and its truth value is False (F).
c) The given sentence is a declarative sentence. So, it is a statement and its truth value is True (T).
d) The given sentence is an interrogative sentence. So, it is not a statement.
e) The given sentence is an imperative sentence. So, it is not a statement.
f) The given sentence is an exclamatory sentence. So, it is not a statement.

questions.text:
Let $p$: demand is increasing and $q$: supply is decreasing. Express each of the following statements into words:
a) $\sim p$
b) $\sim q$
c) $p \land q$
d) $p \lor q$
e) $\sim p \land q$
f) $p \lor \sim q$
g) $\sim p \land \sim q$
h) $\sim(p \land q)$
questions.source_solution:
a) $\sim p$: Demand is not increasing.
b) $\sim q$: Supply is not decreasing.
c) $p \land q$: Demand is increasing and supply is decreasing.
d) $p \lor q$: Demand is increasing or supply is decreasing.
e) $\sim p \land q$: Demand is not increasing and supply is decreasing.
f) $p \lor \sim q$: Demand is increasing or supply is not decreasing.
g) $\sim p \land \sim q$: Neither demand is increasing nor supply is decreasing.
h) $\sim(p \land q)$: It is false that demand is increasing and supply is decreasing.

questions.text:
Express each of the following statements into symbolic form:
a) $p$: temperature is increasing, $q$: length is expanding.
Temperature is increasing and length is expanding.
b) $p$: pressure is decreasing, $q$: volume is increasing.
Pressure is decreasing or volume is increasing.
c) $p$: demand is increasing, $q$: price is increasing.
Neither demand is increasing nor price is increasing.
d) $p$: Pradeep is bold, $q$: Sandeep is handsome.
It is false that Pradeep is bold or Sandeep is handsome.
questions.source_solution:
a) $p \land q$
b) $p \lor q$
c) $\sim p \land \sim q$
d) $\sim(p \lor q)$

questions.text: Construct truth table for: $(\sim p) \land q$
questions.source_solution:
Truth table for $(\sim p) \land q$:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
p & q & \sim p & (\sim p) \land q \\
\hline
T & T & F & F \\
T & F & F & F \\
F & T & T & T \\
F & F & T & F \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

questions.text: Construct truth table for: $(\sim p) \lor (\sim q)$
questions.source_solution:
Truth table for $(\sim p) \lor (\sim q)$:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
p & q & \sim p & \sim q & (\sim p) \lor (\sim q) \\
\hline
T & T & F & F & F \\
T & F & F & T & T \\
F & T & T & F & T \\
F & F & T & T & T \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

questions.text: Construct truth table for: $(p \implies q) \land (q \implies p)$
questions.source_solution:
Truth table for $(p \implies q) \land (q \implies p)$:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
p & q & p \implies q & q \implies p & (p \implies q) \land (q \implies p) \\
\hline
T & T & T & T & T \\
T & F & F & T & F \\
F & T & T & F & F \\
F & F & T & T & T \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

questions.text: If $p$ and $q$ are any two statements, prove that $p \land (\sim p) \equiv c$ where $c$ is a contradiction.
questions.source_solution:
Constructing the truth table for $p \land (\sim p)$:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
p & \sim p & p \land (\sim p) & c \\
\hline
T & F & F & F \\
F & T & F & F \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

From the above truth table, since all truth values in the column $p \land (\sim p)$ are $F$, $p \land (\sim p) \equiv c$.

questions.text: If $p$ and $q$ be the statements. Prove that $p \lor (\sim p \land q)$ is a tautology.
questions.source_solution:
The truth table for $p \lor (\sim p \land q)$ is:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
p & q & \sim p & \sim p \land q & p \lor (\sim p \land q) \\
\hline
T & T & F & F & T \\
T & F & F & F & T \\
F & T & T & T & T \\
F & F & T & F & T \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

Since the truth values of the last column are all $T$, the statement $p \lor (\sim p \land q)$ is a tautology.

Given, $A \cap B = \phi$, so $A$ and $B$ are disjoint sets.
Let $x$ be an arbitrary element of $A$. Then,
$$x \in A \implies x \notin B \quad [\because A \cap B = \phi]$$
$$\implies x \in \overline{B}$$
Hence, $A \subseteq \overline{B}$.

questions.text: If $A \subseteq B$, prove that $A \cup B = B$.
questions.source_solution:
Let $x$ be any arbitrary element of $A \cup B$.
Then, $A \cup B = \{x : x \in A \text{ or } x \in B\}$
$$= \{x : x \in B \text{ or } x \in B\} \quad [\because A \subseteq B]$$
$$= \{x : x \in B\} = B$$
Hence, $A \cup B = B$.

questions.text:
If $A, B$ and $C$ are the subsets of a universal set $U$, prove that:
$$A \cup (B \cap C) = (A \cup B) \cap (A \cup C)$$
questions.source_solution:
Let $x$ be any arbitrary element of $A \cup (B \cap C)$.
Then,
$$x \in A \cup (B \cap C) \iff x \in A \text{ or } (x \in B \cap C)$$
$$\iff x \in A \text{ or } (x \in B \text{ and } x \in C)$$
$$\iff (x \in A \text{ or } x \in B) \text{ and } (x \in A \text{ or } x \in C)$$
$$\iff (x \in A \cup B) \text{ and } (x \in A \cup C)$$
$$\iff x \in (A \cup B) \cap (A \cup C)$$
$$\therefore A \cup (B \cap C) = (A \cup B) \cap (A \cup C)$$

questions.text: If $A, B$ and $C$ are subsets of $U$, prove De Morgan's law: $(A \cup B)' = A' \cap B'$.
questions.source_solution:
Let $x$ be an arbitrary element of $(A \cup B)'$.
Then,
$$x \in $(A \cup B)' \iff x \notin (A \cup B)$$
$$\iff x \notin A \text{ and } x \notin B$$
$$\iff x \in A' \text{ and } x \in B'$$
$$\iff x \in A' \cap B'$$
$$\therefore (A \cup B)' = A' \cap B'$$

The corresponding equation of the inequality $x^2 - 2x > 0$ is:
$$x^2 - 2x = 0 \implies x(x - 2) = 0 \implies x = 0, 2$$

Testing the sign of $x(x - 2)$ across real line intervals:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Intervals} & x & x - 2 & x(x - 2) \\
\hline
(-\infty, 0) & - & - & + \\
(0, 2) & + & - & - \\
(2, \infty) & + & + & + \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

Hence, the required solution set is $x \in (-\infty, 0) \cup (2, \infty)$.
